claim: Research has linked seeing leisure as wasted time with enjoying it less.
evidence_excerpt: the more the participants believed leisure to be wasteful, the less they enjoyed leisure activities.
limitations: Institutional communication, not a full-paper review. Association only; not a universal explanation or demonstrated cause of guilt.

claim: Conditioning self-regard on usefulness may make an unfinished task feel personal for this fictional protagonist.
evidence_excerpt: self-esteem rises and falls around its typical level in response to successes and failures in domains on which one has staked self-worth.
limitations: General theoretical model; the exact work/rest-guilt explanation is not established by the abstract. Narration retains Maybe and If, within an explicit fictional frame.

claim: The fictional character writes a reminder before closing the laptop; no emotional-efficacy claim is made.
evidence_excerpt: Allowing participants to formulate specific plans for their unfulfilled goals eliminated the various activation and interference effects.
limitations: Context only. This abstract concerns measured cognitive effects, not proof that a reminder relieves guilt. The script depicts an action, not a treatment result.
